assumptions: No tolerance was given for frequency, so a default of tol_pct: 2 is used.
No tolerance was given for duty cycle, so a default of tol_abs: 1 percentage point is used.
A 500 ms measurement window is used, giving ~500 periods of the 1 kHz signal for a stable frequency/duty measurement.
Requirement 2 (signal starts on its own after reset) is verified implicitly by measuring the waveform right after the mandatory 1000 ms boot wait, with no stimulus step preceding it.

checks.requirement: The signal on D5 has a frequency of 1 kHz and a duty cycle of 25%, starting on its own right after reset.
checks.feedback: TIMER2 is never cleared when it reaches CC[1] (1000us) — there's no SHORTS_COMPARE1_CLEAR set, so the 16-bit timer keeps counting past 1000 all the way to 65535 ticks (~65.5 ms) before wrapping to 0, where it then re-triggers the two PPI/GPIOTE toggles. That gives a real period of ~65.5 ms (~15.3 Hz), matching the measured 15.426 Hz. Add 'NRF_TIMER2->SHORTS = TIMER_SHORTS_COMPARE1_CLEAR_Msk;' after setting CC[1] (around line 43) so the timer resets to 0 at the end of each 1000us period.

checks.requirement: The signal on D5 has a frequency of 1 kHz and a duty cycle of 25%, starting on its own right after reset.
checks.feedback: Because the timer is never cleared at CC[1] (missing TIMER_SHORTS_COMPARE1_CLEAR), the pin toggles low at 250us and back high at 1000us as intended, but then stays high for the remaining ~64536us until the 16-bit timer wraps around and finally reaches CC[0]/CC[1] again. That makes the pin high for the vast majority of the (much longer) actual period, producing the measured ~98.86% duty cycle instead of 25%. Adding the missing SHORTS to clear TIMER2 on COMPARE[1] (near line 43, after CC[0]/CC[1] setup) will restore the correct 250us-high/750us-low pattern.

checks.requirement: The signal on D5 has a frequency of 1 kHz and a duty cycle of 25%, starting on its own right after reset.
Must use a hardware timer/PWM peripheral (not analogWrite() or delay()-based bit-banging).
checks.reason: Not electrically observable: a correctly timed 1 kHz/25% waveform can be produced by either a hardware timer or careful software timing; this can only be checked by TA code review.

checks.requirement: Register values/constants are commented and their computation explained.
checks.reason: Code documentation/comments cannot be verified electrically; requires manual review of the submitted source.
